blocks.text: PROPHET AND LAST JUDGE OF ISRAEL · THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL
Samuel. Judged Israel all his life from Ramah, and anointed its first two kings.
LED ISRAELi
Not given "Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life"; no number of years is given
TRIBE
Levi in 1 Chronicles 6; his father is called an Ephrathite of mount Ephraim (1 Samuel 1:1)
IN THE LINE
15th of 15

PROPHETS
Samuel himself · The company of the prophets
THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
THE CYCLE
Forgetting, oppression, a cry, a deliverer, rest
1 · FORGOT GOD Israel had "strange gods and Ashtaroth" among them; at Samuel's word "the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the LORD only". 1 Samuel 7:3–4
2 · OPPRESSED: THE PHILISTINES The Philistines had taken the ark and Israel's cities; when Israel gathered at Mizpeh, their lords went up against them. 1 Samuel 4:11 1 Samuel 7:7 1 Samuel 7:14
3 · CRIED OUT Israel fasted and confessed "We have sinned", and begged Samuel "Cease not to cry unto the LORD our God for us". 1 Samuel 7:6 1 Samuel 7:8
4 · DELIVERED As Samuel offered a lamb, "the LORD thundered with a great thunder" on the Philistines; "they came no more into the coast of Israel". 1 Samuel 7:9–13
5 · REST Scripture does not say.
ACCESSION
How Samuel came to power
Hannah named him Samuel, "Because I have asked him of the LORD", and lent him to the LORD at Shiloh. 1 Samuel 1:20 1 Samuel 1:24–28
"The child did minister unto the LORD before Eli the priest." 1 Samuel 2:11 1 Samuel 2:18
The LORD called him by night: "Speak; for thy servant heareth." 1 Samuel 3:4–10
"The word of Samuel came to all Israel." 1 Samuel 4:1
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"The LORD was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground"; all Israel "knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD". 1 Samuel 3:19–20
He went yearly in circuit to Beth-el, Gilgal and Mizpeh, and judged Israel at home in Ramah. 1 Samuel 7:15–17
At the end, he asked the people to witness against him, and they answered "Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us". 1 Samuel 12:3–5
"God forbid that I should sin against the LORD in ceasing to pray for you." 1 Samuel 12:23
Later Scripture sets him beside Moses as one who called on the LORD and stood before him. Psalms 99:6 Jeremiah 15:1
Peter counts the prophets "from Samuel"; Paul says God gave judges "until Samuel the prophet". Acts 3:24 Acts 13:20
"The acts of David the king ... are written in the book of Samuel the seer." 1 Chronicles 29:29
His sons, made judges in Beer-sheba, "walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes". 1 Samuel 8:1–3

No later Passover was like Josiah's "from the days of Samuel the prophet". 2 Chronicles 35:18

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given
Scripture gives no length for Samuel's judgeship and no year BC. Twenty years passed between the ark's return and the assembly at Mizpeh (1 Samuel 7:2).
Joel; his name has dropped out of 1 Chronicles 6:28
Keil (1872)
Keil holds that the name of the firstborn, Joel, is missing from the verse, as 1 Chronicles 6:33 and 1 Samuel 8:2 show. The site's person data likewise attaches 1 Chronicles 6:28 to Joel.[13]
Vashni, as the KJV prints it
The KJV translators' reading of the verse
The KJV renders the verse as a name, "the firstborn Vashni". 1 Chronicles 6:28

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no number of years for Samuel's judgeship and no year BC.
In 1 Samuel 12:11 (KJV) Samuel names himself among the deliverers; Keil reports that the Syriac, the Arabic and one Greek manuscript read Samson there.
Samuel is never called king; he gave up his place to Saul but went on judging and prophesying (1 Samuel 12:1-2; 7:15).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
Chronicles places Samuel ("Shemuel") in the Levite line of Kohath, as father of Joel and grandfather of the singer Heman. 1 Chronicles 6:22–28 1 Chronicles 6:33–38
